proposed_edits.source_excerpt: For $n\ge2$, a randomized classical algorithm that samples three distinct addresses uniformly without replacement and outputs constant exactly when all three replies agree has success probability at least $3/4$ on every Deutsch–Jozsa input.
proposed_edits.proposed_replacement: For $n\ge2$, the finite probability experiment that samples three distinct addresses uniformly without replacement and outputs constant exactly when all three replies agree has success probability at least $3/4$ on every Deutsch–Jozsa input. In the finite fair-bit classical query model, sampling three independent uniform addresses with replacement and using the same output rule also succeeds with probability at least $3/4$, using exactly $3n$ random bits and three value queries.

proposed_edits.source_excerpt: On a balanced input the procedure errs only on the event in step 1.1, so its success is at least $3/4$.
proposed_edits.proposed_replacement: The without-replacement experiment has success at least $3/4$ by step 1.1. For an implementation in the finite fair-bit model, take three independent blocks of $n$ fair bits as addresses, allowing repetitions. On a balanced input each reply is an independent fair bit, so all three replies agree with probability $2(1/2)^3=1/4$; on a constant input they always agree. Thus this three-query algorithm also has success at least $3/4$.
